v1.description: Ask the Digital Health Platform for patient data for a research study.

proposal.label: research proposal
proposal.description: Optional. Upload your research proposal or protocol, as a PDF or Word document, and the study information and dates below are filled in from it for you to check.

intake.label: Intake questionnaire
intake.description: The data your study needs, and how you will look after it.

study.title: Study information
study.description: About the study this request is for. These answers fill in your research plan.

studyTitle.text: What is the title of your study?
studyTitle.purpose: The title of the research plan, and how the request is known
studyTitle.extractionPrompt: Find the study's full title, as given on the cover page or at the head of the synopsis. Quote it exactly, without the word 'Title' or a protocol number.

piName.purpose: Who is accountable for the study and its data
piName.extractionPrompt: Find the name of the principal or lead investigator, usually on the cover page, the study team page or the signature page. Give the person's name only, with any degree such as Dr. or PhD as written.

piTitle.text: What is the Principal Investigator's title?
piTitle.description: For example: Scientist, Toronto General Hospital Research Institute.
piTitle.purpose: The Principal Investigator's position, as the research plan states it
piTitle.extractionPrompt: Find the principal investigator's position and institution, as stated next to their name, for example 'Scientist, Toronto General Hospital Research Institute'. Give only what the document states.

piContact.text: How can we reach the Principal Investigator?
piContact.description: Their department address, email and phone number.
piContact.purpose: Reaching the Principal Investigator about the request
piContact.extractionPrompt: Find the principal investigator's contact details: department address, email address and phone number, as given in the document. Give whichever of these it states, on one line.

coInvestigators.description: The name and role of each. Leave this blank if there are none.
coInvestigators.purpose: Everyone else on the study team who works with the data
coInvestigators.extractionPrompt: List the co-investigators or sub-investigators named in the study team, each with their role when it is stated, separated by semicolons. Leave out the principal investigator. If the document names none, report that the answer was not found.

background.text: What are the background and objectives of your study?
background.description: A short summary of why the study is being done and what it aims to find out.
background.purpose: Why the study is being done, as the research plan summarizes it
background.extractionPrompt: Summarize the study's background and its primary objective in two or three sentences, from the background, rationale and objectives sections.

analysis.text: How will you analyze the data?
analysis.description: Briefly describe your statistical analysis or methodology.
analysis.purpose: Whether the data asked for fits the analysis planned
analysis.extractionPrompt: Summarize the planned statistical analysis or methodology in one or two sentences, from the statistics, analysis or methods section.

references.description: Protocol or literature references, if any.
references.purpose: The sources the research plan cites
references.extractionPrompt: List up to five of the main references the document cites, each in short form (first author, year, title), separated by semicolons. If it has no reference list, report that the answer was not found.

sources.text: Where will the data for your study come from?
sources.description: Choose the main place your data is coming from. If you are using more than one source, select all that apply.

uhn.label: UHN internal data (e.g., UHN patient health records accessed through the Digital Health Platform (DHP), JDMI)

capcrId.text: What is the CAPCR ID of the other UHN study?

repositoryDetails.text: Which shared data repository? Give its name and a brief description.

hasMrnList.text: Do you already have a list of specific patients (by Medical Record Number, or MRN) whose data you need?
hasMrnList.description: An MRN list is a list of the hospital ID numbers for the exact patients you want included — for example, patients already enrolled in your study. Do not upload the list now; we will ask for it in a later step.

yes.label: Yes
yes.description: You will be asked to securely provide your MRN list later. Do not email it or upload it here.

groupTypes.text: Which group of patients is your study about?
groupTypes.description: Select all that describe your group. Examples: adults with heart failure; patients who received a liver transplant; patients seen in the stroke clinic; patients receiving immunotherapy for lung cancer.

disease.label: A disease or condition (e.g., heart failure, type 2 diabetes)

procedure.label: A procedure or surgery (e.g., liver transplant, knee replacement)

program.label: A program or clinic (e.g., stroke clinic)

treatment.label: A treatment or exposure (e.g., chemotherapy, a specific medication)

provider.label: A care provider or service (e.g., patients seen by cardiology)

groupDescription.description: If you chose Other above, this description is your main answer.

findBy.text: How can we find the patients who fit your study?
findBy.description: Tell us about the specific details in the health record that show a patient belongs in your group. Examples: a diagnosis code (e.g., ICD-10 I50 for heart failure); a medication (e.g., patients who received pembrolizumab); a lab result (e.g., HbA1c above 8%); a type of visit (e.g., emergency department visits). If you don't know the exact codes, describe what you're looking for.

visit.label: Type or location of visit (e.g., inpatient stay, ED visit, specific clinic)

unsure.label: I'm not sure — I need help defining this
unsure.description: A data analyst will help you define this. It does not stop you from sending your request.

findByDiagnosis.text: Which diagnoses? Give the codes if you know them.

findByProcedure.text: Which procedures? Give the codes if you know them.

findByVisit.text: Which type or location of visit?

findByOther.text: What other details in the health record show a patient belongs in your group?

limitSites.text: Should your study include only patients seen at certain UHN hospitals, programs, or departments?
limitSites.description: Answer "No" if patients from any UHN location can be included. Example of "Yes": only patients treated at a specific location or only patients seen in a specific clinic.

no.label: No — include patients from all UHN locations

sites.text: Which UHN hospitals, programs, or departments?

hasExclusions.text: Are there any patients who should be left out of your study?
hasExclusions.description: These are patients who would otherwise fit your group but should not be included. Examples: patients under 18; patients who are immunocompromised; patients with a previous cancer diagnosis.

exclusionTypes.text: Which patients should be left out?
exclusionTypes.description: Select all that apply, then describe each.

excludeAge.text: Which ages should be left out?

excludePriorDiagnosis.text: Which previous diagnoses should leave a patient out?

excludeConditions.text: Which other health conditions should leave a patient out?

excludeOther.text: Which other patients should be left out?

timePeriod.title: Time period and frequency
timePeriod.description: Only data from within these dates will be included. Example: 2018-01-01 to 2024-12-31 includes visits, tests, and other records dated between those two days.

startDate.text: Start date: what is the earliest date to include?
startDate.description: This cannot be in the future.
startDate.purpose: The earliest records the data pull includes
startDate.extractionPrompt: Find the start of the period whose patient records the study reviews or collects, such as the first admission or visit date of a retrospective chart review. This is the period of the data, not when the study itself runs. If the document gives only a month or a year, report that the answer was not found.

endDate.text: End date: what is the latest date to include?
endDate.description: This must be on or after the start date.
endDate.purpose: The latest records the data pull includes
endDate.extractionPrompt: Find the end of the period whose patient records the study reviews or collects. This is the period of the data, not when the study itself ends. If the document gives only a month or a year, report that the answer was not found.

frequency.text: Do you need this data once, or on a repeating schedule?
frequency.description: Choose "one time" if you need a single copy of the data. Choose "repeating" if you need updated data sent to you regularly during your study. Please note: repeating requests take longer to set up.

repeating.label: Repeating (recurring)
repeating.description: The data must then be saved in a secure UHN-approved location.

interval.text: How often do you need updated data?
interval.description: Example: monthly updates to track new patients enrolled in your study.

intervalOther.text: Describe how often you need updated data.

stopMonth.text: When do you expect to stop needing recurring data?
stopMonth.description: Give the month and year as YYYY-MM, for example 2027-06. An estimate is fine. This is usually when your study's data collection ends. This can be updated later if this date changes.
stopMonth.patternMessage: Give the month and year as YYYY-MM, for example 2027-06.

waiver.text: Will you use patient data without asking each patient for their consent?
waiver.description: If your study will use data from patients who have not agreed to take part, you need permission from the Research Ethics Board (REB) to do this. This is called a "waiver of consent."

yes.label: Yes — I am requesting a waiver of consent

no.label: No — all patients have given, or will give, consent

waiverCriteria.title: Requirements for a waiver of consent
waiverCriteria.description: For each requirement, answer Yes or No, then briefly explain why. Example of a strong explanation: "Contacting 12,000 patients seen over 10 years is not practical, and many are no longer reachable." If you answer No to any of them, the waiver may not be granted: contact the Research Ethics Board (REB) before sending your request.

minimalRisk.text: The research involves no more than minimal risk to the participants.

minimalRiskWhy.text: Explain your answer about minimal risk.

welfare.text: The waiver of informed consent is unlikely to adversely affect the welfare of participants.

welfareWhy.text: Explain your answer about the welfare of participants.

impracticable.text: It is impossible or impracticable to carry out the research and to address the research question properly, given the research design, if the prior consent of participants is required.
impracticable.description: See the TCPS 2 glossary for what "impracticable" means: https://ethics.gc.ca/eng/tcps2-eptc2_2022_glossary-glossaire.html

impracticableWhy.text: Explain your answer about asking for prior consent.

secondaryUse.text: Research relies exclusively on secondary use of non-identifiable data.

secondaryUseWhy.text: Explain your answer about secondary use of non-identifiable data.

level.text: How much patient-identifying information do you need?
level.description: Choose the option that gives you the least identifying information while still letting you complete your study. Less identifying data usually means a faster review.

deidentified.label: De-identified
deidentified.description: No names, ID numbers, or other details that could reveal who a patient is.

coded.label: Coded
coded.description: Names and ID numbers are replaced with a study code. A separate, secured key links each code back to the patient.

identifiable.label: Identifiable
identifiable.description: Includes names, ID numbers, or other details that show who a patient is.

identifiers.text: Which identifying details do you need?
identifiers.description: Select only what your study needs, then say why you need each one. Example: "Date of birth — needed to calculate exact age at diagnosis."

whyName.text: Why do you need patient names?

whyMrn.text: Why do you need Medical Record Numbers?

whyHealthCard.text: Why do you need health card numbers?

whyBirthDate.text: Why do you need dates of birth?

whyPostalCode.text: Why do you need postal codes?

whyVisitDates.text: Why do you need the dates of visits or procedures?

otherIdentifiers.text: Which other identifying details do you need, and why?

combine.text: Will you combine this data with data from somewhere else?
combine.description: Examples: a disease registry; data from another hospital; information your study team collected directly from participants (e.g., survey responses).

otherSources.text: What is the other data source, and who owns it?
otherSources.description: Example: "Ontario Cancer Registry, owned by Ontario Health." If there is more than one source, put each one on a line of its own.

matchOn.text: What information will you use to match the same patient across the data sources?
matchOn.description: Example: health card number, or a combination of date of birth and postal code. Any identifier you pick here should also be among the identifying details you asked for under Patient identity.

matchOnOther.text: What other information will you use to match patients?

matcher.description: This is the person or team who will combine the datasets.

matcherOutside.text: Who outside UHN will match the data? Name the person or organization.

workLocations.text: Where will you open and work with the data?
workLocations.description: Select every place where the data will be viewed or analyzed.

hpc.label: HPC for Health (UHN's high-performance computing environment)

uhnComputer.label: A UHN computer connected to the UHN network

uhnServer.label: A UHN server connected to the UHN network

workOutside.text: Where outside UHN will you open and work with the data?

workOther.text: Which other place will you open and work with the data in?

storage.text: Where will the data be saved?
storage.description: Give the exact system, drive, or folder. Example: "UHN shared drive: \\[server]\StudyName\Data." Note: if you selected a repeating data request, the data must be saved in a secure UHN-approved location.

external.text: Will anyone outside UHN be able to see or receive this data?
external.description: Examples: sharing data with a study sponsor or collaborator at another institution; accessing the data through a system hosted outside UHN.

externalDetails.text: Who outside UHN will receive or access the data, and how?

policyConfirm.text: I confirm that I will follow UHN policy for storing, moving, and destroying this data.
policyConfirm.description: Administrative: Management, Retention & Destruction of UHN Records policy 1.30.007, at https://documents.uhn.ca/sites/uhn/Policies/administrative/legal_affairs/1.30.007-doc.pdf

researchPlan.label: Research plan
researchPlan.description: Filled in from your answers when you send the request. You can preview it first, or upload your own version as a .docx to be sent instead.
